import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from lets_plot import *

GITHACK_JS_URL = 'https://glcdn.githack.com/gr13nka-group/lets-plot/raw/iter10-squash/js-package/distr/lets-plot.min.js'

# Load the iter10-squash frontend bundle through GitHack, while keeping the local
# Python API/kernel used to produce the plot specs.
LetsPlot.set({'js_url_manual': GITHACK_JS_URL})
LetsPlot.setup_html(offline=False)
In [2]:
# The registered style names (plot-builder/.../defaultTheme/DrawingStyles.kt).
# Adding a style there makes it appear here with no other change.
STYLES = ['crisp', 'xkcd']


def styles(p, w=290, h=210):
    """Render one plot spec once per drawing style, side by side.

    The plot `p` carries NO style of its own: the same spec goes through every style,
    which is the whole point - a geom cannot tell which style will draw it.
    """
    return gggrid(
        [p + theme(geom_style=s) + ggtitle(s) + ggsize(w, h) for s in STYLES],
        ncol=len(STYLES),
    )

penguins = pd.read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JetBrains/lets-plot-docs/master/data/penguins.csv').dropna().sort_values('bill_length_mm')

# Per-species summary - feeds the interval geoms (errorbar / linerange / pointrange / crossbar / lollipop).
summ = penguins.groupby('species', as_index=False).agg(m=('body_mass_g', 'mean'), s=('body_mass_g', 'std'))
summ['ymin'] = summ['m'] - summ['s']
summ['ymax'] = summ['m'] + summ['s']

# A binned ordered series - feeds the path / ribbon / step family.
# (drop the Interval bin column: pandas' interval dtype is not a plottable type)
band = (penguins.assign(_b=pd.cut(penguins['bill_length_mm'], bins=16))
        .groupby('_b', as_index=False, observed=True)
        .agg(x=('bill_length_mm', 'mean'), m=('body_mass_g', 'mean'), s=('body_mass_g', 'std'))
        .drop(columns='_b')
        .dropna())
band['ymin'] = band['m'] - band['s']
band['ymax'] = band['m'] + band['s']

       + geom_point(size=3)
       + geom_text(size=9, nudge_y=0.25)
       + geom_label(size=7, nudge_y=-0.25))

# A geometry-only style varies geometry and nothing else: same colours, same fonts, same glyphs.
p = ggplot(penguins, aes('species', 'body_mass_g', fill='species')) + geom_boxplot()
gggrid([
    p + theme(geom_style='xkcd') + ggtitle('xkcd'),
    p + theme(geom_style='xkcd', text=element_text(family='Georgia')) + ggtitle('user font still applies'),
], ncol=2) + ggsize(700, 260)

In [45]:
# Interactive pan check for the wobble seed.
# Drag to pan (toolbar via ggtb): each geom's xkcd wobble should ride WITH the shape,
# not re-randomize ("boil") frame to frame - the seed is the data point index, not the
# client-space coordinates. Zoom reorganizes the wobble but also does not boil.
(ggplot(band, aes('x', 'm'))
 + geom_area(fill='#a1d99b', color='#31a354', alpha=0.5, size=1)
 + geom_line(size=1.2, color='#2b8cbe')
 + geom_point(size=3, color='#2b8cbe')
 + theme(geom_style='xkcd')
 + ggsize(900, 500)
 + ggtb())
Out[45]:
